evidence_type: core operation and standalone preference-save timing probes; not end-to-end UI latency
core_workload: One new process; sequential 48k stereo, 96k stereo, 48k stereo A/B cases. A new Capture per case, 600 seconds of constant 0.05f32 audio batched in 10ms blocks.
core_quantiles: Nearest sorted observation at round((n-1)*q); for n=20 median is the upper central observation, not the average of two central values.
limitations: Initial local harness and official example run are separate observations; workload/case/stage counts match, but system load and CPU frequency were uncontrolled.
Per-stage n=1 timings are single observations, not independent repeated-run distributions.
Snapshot copy is one lane, not a complete A/B WAV export.
The 180-to-30 stage follows a limit increase to 600 without refilling discarded audio; retained content is still 180 seconds.
Warm 1000 expand/shrink pairs operate on already-shortened content, not repeatedly refilled ten-minute buffers.
Fresh process/directories do not establish cold boot, paging, storage-device or antivirus causes.
Preference timings include the full production save call; controller enums in the standalone harness are parsing/default stand-ins.
No GUI/DAW/GPU/device audio or audible-artifact validation is performed by these probes.
Historical 2026-11-14-windows traces and hashes remain separate and unchanged.
Asynchronous writer measurement predates later queue-drain/coalescing and review changes; recorded historical production source hash is not a final-binary latency guarantee.

Native functional observations refer to an intermediate build; final copy-cleanup/resize and payload-integrity observations are recorded separately in final-builds.json. Neither establishes broad macOS/DAW/physical Shift-drag or new-payload installation acceptance.
